summary: An empty `cerca` whose window reaches recent days measures that archive on the spot and names the date the source stops at, instead of declaring a hardcoded 9-45 day band. It speaks when the window reaches past the measured frontier and stays silent when the source has already published beyond it; the probe carries the search's structural filters, so a query on one committee reports that committee's frontier.
reason: `latenzaFonteGiorni = 45` did two jobs with one number: it gated the hint and it told the user the portal publishes "9-45 days late". Measured on 2026-09-18 across all twelve archives the real lag ran from 2 days (resoconti, sommari) to 58 (risoluzioni), so the band was wrong at both ends, and as a threshold it silenced the hint on risoluzioni and odg where it was needed most. The original note said attaching `sync coverage` would cost a live request per call; it costs one request only on an empty result whose window is recent, which is the one case where the answer changes what the reader concludes. Archive-level coverage was not enough on its own: on 2026-09-16 the sommari archive was 2 days behind while its QUARTA committee was 10.
validated_outcome: Unit tests with a fixed clock cover both directions: a window past the frontier speaks, one inside the published range stays silent, a failed measurement still warns without a figure, and archives whose frontier cannot be measured (pareri, biblioteca) stay silent rather than pointing at a non-measurement. Text filters must not appear in the probe params nor in the hint's prose, since they are not measured. Live with the installed binary: `commissioni sommari --commissione QUARTA --data 2026-09-16` reports the archive stopping on 2026-09-08, 10 days, where it used to say "9-45 days"; `ddl cerca --data 2026-09-17` reports 4 days, where the band claimed at least 9; `risoluzioni cerca --data 2026-08-01` reports 58 days, where the 45-day threshold used to silence it entirely. `--anno` counts as a window only on archives that have no `--data` at all, which is `leggi`, and its aggregated branch now goes through the hint: `leggi cerca --anno 2026 --numero 40` warns where it used to answer [] in silence, while `ddl cerca --anno 2026 --numero 99999` stays silent, since a year published through 14 September is not latency. The probe uses a fresh session, since a reused one continues the search instead of repeating it, and gives up as soon as the first page is truncated on a source whose order does not descend: leggi went from 16.5s spent and discarded to 6.2s. Live gate after the change: 127/127, 0 fail. Review follow-up (PR #2019): the probe walks back to prior years when the current one is empty, as far as `sync coverage` does, since an archive far behind in January has its newest record in December and stopping at the current year would drop the figure exactly when the lag is largest; the two numbers must agree, because the hint sends the reader to that command. An empty year only licenses looking further back when the page was read to the end: a year that could not be read stops the walk, since otherwise an older year's frontier would be passed off as the latest. Unit tests on that decision table; live re-check shows sommari/QUARTA, ddl, risoluzioni and leggi unchanged.
